item.title: Women VDGs guard Jammu’s remote villages during winters as men migrate for livelihood
item.description: Jammu: Women Village Defence Guards (VDGs) are safeguarding remote villages of the Jammu region during the winter months, when many men migrate to other parts of the country in search of livelihood. Equipped with .303 rifles after undergoing training provided by various security agencies, the women members of VDGs are deployed in difficult terrain, often in isolated and vulnerable areas, Superintendent of Police Bhaderwah Vinod Sharma said. item.title: Colder than Kashmir: Jammu freezes at 7.4°C, records 4th coldest day in decades
item.description: Jammu: Jammu on Wednesday reeled under an unusually harsh winter spell, recording one of its coldest days in decades and emerging colder than several high-altitude locations in the Kashmir Valley, as dense fog disrupted normal life and transport across the plains. The city registered a maximum temperature of just 7.4 degrees Celsius, nearly 10 degrees below the seasonal average, making it the fourth-lowest daytime temperature recorded in Jammu in the past four decades. item.title: Jammu Kashmir Shivers as Cold Wave Continues
item.description: Srinagar, Jan 15: Jammu and Kashmir continued to reel under severe cold, with most parts of the Kashmir Valley recording sub-zero temperatures, while several areas in the Jammu region experienced chilly nights. item.title: Cop dies of Cardiac arrest at PCR Srinagar
item.description: Srinagar,Jan 15: A police personnel died of a suspected cardiac arrest at the Police Control Room (PCR) in Srinagar on Thursday, officials said. An official stated that the officer, posted with the IR 6th Battalion at PCR Srinagar, was found unconscious in his room. He was immediately taken to the PCR hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival. “The preliminary cause of death appears to be cardiac arrest,” the official added. item.title: Class 12th Student found dead hours after Board exam results in Jammu Kashmir
item.description: Srinagar,Jan 15: A 17-year-old Class 12 student from Doda district of Jammu and Kashmir was found dead yesterday, hours after the declaration of the board examination results. The deceased has been identified as Revansh Sharma, a resident of Paryote village in Doda district. He had appeared in the Class 12 examinations this year and had reportedly failed in the Economics subject. According to available information, the student became distressed after checking his result and was later found dead.
